note_en: 连…都 means "even" and marks the most extreme case: 连走廊里都站着人 "people were standing even in the aisles." English can put "even" almost anywhere, but in Chinese 连 goes right before the surprising item and 都 (or 也) has to come before the verb. Leave out 都 and the sentence sounds unfinished.
